# Recreation Prompt

Build a mobile-first browser canvas game called **Dead Tide: The Ninth Break**. Preserve the source mechanic: the player drags backward from an idle circular projectile, releases to launch with gravity, scores when the projectile falls through a target opening on the right, resets after scoring, and loses when the projectile settles on the floor. Rebuild the surface as a dramatic surf-beach creepypasta legend. The projectile is a glowing cursed surf relic, the target is a hollow spectral wave, the score is Hollow Breaks, and the failure fantasy is the wet sand reclaiming the relic. Use procedural moonlit beach art, animated wave lines, ghost foam, cliffs, rocks, and sigil UI. Keep the implementation self-contained in `index.html` using HTML/CSS/Canvas/vanilla JS.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile-first one-shot drag-launch arcade physics game.
- objective: pull the ball/relic backward and release so it passes downward through the target opening.
- input model: mouse or touch starts on the canvas only while the projectile is idle, drag sets opposite launch vector, release fires.
- core loop: start game, idle projectile waits at lower-left, aim preview appears while dragging, projectile flies with gravity and wall bounce, crossing the target line while falling increments score and resets a new target, settling on the floor ends the run, restart repeats.
- fail/friction state: floor bounce applies damping/friction; when velocity falls below thresholds the game-over panel appears.

## Protected mechanics
- Canvas runtime and requestAnimationFrame update cadence.
- Drag-back-to-launch input semantics on mouse and touch.
- Gravity value 0.6, drag power 0.18, max launch power 25.
- Projectile start near lower-left, target on right side, score only when falling through target opening.
- Wall bounce, floor bounce/friction, backboard/target-side rebound, score reset delay, game-over/restart state flow.

## Remixed target
Dead Tide: The Ninth Break reframes the projectile as a cursed surf relic, the hoop as a haunted hollow wave, the court as a moonlit beach, score as Hollow Breaks, and failure as the legend reclaiming the relic. Mechanics are preserved while identity, HUD language, procedural background, focal silhouette, feedback copy, and presentation become a dramatic surf-beach creepypasta legend.
